action.label: Policy Action
action.description: The action the service took on the transaction (Allowed, Blocked).

reason.label: Policy Reason
reason.description: The action taken and, for blocks, the policy applied.

rulelabel.label: Blocked Policy Name
rulelabel.description: The rule applied to the transaction. Populated only for Block rules.

ruletype.label: Blocked Policy Type
ruletype.description: The type of policy that blocked. Populated only for Block rules.

urlfilterrulelabel.label: URL Filtering Policy Name
urlfilterrulelabel.description: The URL Filtering rule applied to the transaction.

apprulelabel.label: Cloud Application Policy Name
apprulelabel.description: The Cloud App Control rule applied to the transaction.

appname.label: Cloud Application
appname.description: The cloud application of the transaction.

urlcat.label: URL Category
urlcat.description: The category of the destination URL.

urlcatmethod.description: The source of the URL's category (for example Database A).

subjects.title: Which rule decided a web transaction, from the logs

claims.statement: `urlcat` records the category the transaction was judged under, and `urlcatmethod` records where that categorization came from, which is how logs reveal a URL's actual category membership.
`rulelabel` and `ruletype` are filled only when a Block rule applied; an allowed transaction has neither, so an empty `rulelabel` does not mean no rule matched.

URL Filtering and Cloud App Control each have their own rule-name field (`urlfilterrulelabel`, `apprulelabel`), so one record can name both when both layers evaluated, and the allow-side rule is visible there even when `rulelabel` is empty.
The `*rulelabel` fields of the NSS web log carry the name of the rule that applied, not a Rule Label object; the field list shows no field for rule labels.
